practiceQuestions.q: When was the National Health Mission (NHM), which subsumed the National Rural Health Mission and the National Urban Health Mission, officially launched?
practiceQuestions.sol: The National Health Mission (NHM) was approved by the Union Cabinet on May 1, 2013, subsuming the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) and the newly launched National Urban Health Mission (NUHM). NRHM was originally launched in 2005.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the annual financial coverage per family provided under the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)?
practiceQuestions.sol: AB-PMJAY provides a health cover of Rs. 5 Lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization across public and empanelled private hospitals in India.

practiceQuestions.q: Which portal/platform was launched under Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) to create a unique health ID for every citizen in India?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under ABDM, an Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) number is generated, which is a 14-digit number that uniquely identifies citizens and links their digital health records.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary objective of the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA)?
opts: Providing assured, comprehensive and quality antenatal care free of cost on the 9th of every month
Providing cash incentives for institutional deliveries
Nutritional support to pregnant and lactating mothers
practiceQuestions.sol: PMSMA guarantees a minimum package of qualitative antenatal care services to pregnant women on the 9th day of every month by obstetricians/medical officers at designated health facilities.

practiceQuestions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) focuses primarily on which aspect of public health?
opts: Providing health insurance to BPL families
Filling critical gaps in public health infrastructure, especially in critical care and primary care
Providing generic medicines at subsidized rates
practiceQuestions.sol: PM-ABHIM is one of the largest pan-India schemes for strengthening healthcare infrastructure across primary, secondary, and tertiary care, enhancing disease surveillance, and building capacity for detecting and curing new and emerging diseases.

practiceQuestions.q: Mission Indradhanush, launched by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, aims to achieve full immunization coverage for which demographic group?
opts: Children up to 2 years of age and pregnant women
practiceQuestions.sol: Mission Indradhanush targets children up to 2 years of age and pregnant women who have been unvaccinated or partially vaccinated against vaccine-preventable diseases.

practiceQuestions.q: Under the Pradhan Mantri Bharatiya Jan Aushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP), what kind of stores are established to make quality medicines available at affordable prices?
practiceQuestions.sol: PMBJP establishes dedicated outlets known as 'Jan Aushadhi Kendras' to provide generic medicines that are comparable in quality and efficacy to expensive branded drugs.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary focus of the 'Ayushman Arogya Mandir' initiative, which rebranded the former Ayushman Bharat-Health and Wellness Centres (AB-HWCs)?
opts: Delivering Comprehensive Primary Health Care (CPHC) closer to the community
Managing national disease control programs remotely
Issuing medical insurance cards to citizens
practiceQuestions.sol: Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (formerly HWCs) focus on delivering Comprehensive Primary Health Care (CPHC), bringing healthcare services closer to the homes of people, covering both maternal-child health and non-communicable diseases.

practiceQuestions.q: The National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP) deals with the prevention and control of vector-borne diseases. Which of the following is NOT typically covered under it?
practiceQuestions.sol: Tuberculosis is a bacterial infectious disease handled by the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP), whereas malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Japanese encephalitis, and lymphatic filariasis are vector-borne diseases covered under NVBDCP.

practiceQuestions.q: Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi (RAN) provides financial assistance to which category of patients?
opts: All citizens suffering from any ailment
Patients living below the poverty line (BPL) suffering from major life-threatening diseases
Only senior citizens requiring geriatric care
Children suffering from rare genetic disorders only
practiceQuestions.sol: Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi (RAN) provides financial assistance to patients living below the poverty line (BPL) who are suffering from major life-threatening diseases, for treatment at major government hospitals.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the decentralized architecture of the National Health Mission (NHM) enhance public health governance compared to centralized top-down schemes?
opts: By completely eliminating the role of state governments in policy formulation
Through District Health Action Plans (DHAPs) that empower local bodies to address region-specific disease burdens
By delegating all financial resource allocation exclusively to private corporate partners
By relying solely on international donor funding without domestic accountability
practiceQuestions.sol: NHM promotes decentralized planning through District Health Action Plans (DHAPs). This allows districts to tailor public health interventions based on local epidemiological profiles, socio-economic contexts, and resource constraints rather than a uniform one-size-fits-all approach.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary difference in the operational models between Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY and traditional supply-side public health provisioning?
opts: PM-JAY focuses on demand-side financing through health insurance, whereas traditional models focus on direct provisioning through public hospitals
PM-JAY is exclusively for primary care, while traditional models handle tertiary care
PM-JAY is fully funded by foreign direct investments, while traditional models are funded by cess
There is no functional difference; both operate identically
practiceQuestions.sol: PM-JAY represents a paradigm shift from 'supply-side' financing (building government hospitals and stocking medicines) to 'demand-side' financing (providing portability of insurance to purchase care from both public and empanelled private providers).

practiceQuestions.q: How does the 'Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission' (ABDM) address information asymmetry and fragmentation in India's healthcare sector?
opts: By mandating private hospitals to share 50% of their revenues with the government
By creating a federated architecture that links electronic health records (EHR) securely across providers using unique ABHA IDs
By replacing all paper prescriptions with printed barcodes managed solely by AI algorithms
By centralizing all patient health data into a single mega server managed by NITI Aayog
practiceQuestions.sol: ABDM does not store medical records centrally; instead, it uses a federated architecture where health records remain with respective healthcare providers. ABHA and Health Data Locker enable seamless, consent-based sharing of records across different facilities.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the systemic rationale behind integrating AYUSH (Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy) infrastructure into the National Health Mission?
opts: To completely phase out modern allopathic medicine in rural areas
To leverage pluralistic healthcare practices, mainstream traditional systems, and provide cost-effective options for preventive and primary care
To divert central funds away from allopathic infrastructure towards commercial export of herbs
To establish mandatory traditional medicine degrees for all civil servants
practiceQuestions.sol: Integrating AYUSH under NHM (AYUSH mainstreaming) aims to utilize local health traditions and rich indigenous systems for preventive and promotive healthcare, reduce out-of-pocket expenditure, and offer choices to patients within public health facilities.

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of public health economics, how do schemes like Pradhan Mantri Bharatiya Jan Aushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) mitigate 'Catastrophic Health Expenditure' (CHE)?
opts: By directly paying cash to households to buy private health insurance
By lowering out-of-pocket expenditure on essential medicines, which often forms the highest share of recurring household medical expenses
By imposing price ceilings on private hospital surgical procedures
By offering tax rebates to pharmaceutical companies manufacturing lifestyle drugs
practiceQuestions.sol: Out-of-pocket expenditure (OOPE) on medicines accounts for a major portion of healthcare spending in India, pushing millions into poverty. PMBJP provides unbranded generic equivalents at 50-90% lower prices, directly easing the financial burden of chronic illnesses.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the strategic significance of transforming Sub-Health Centres and Primary Health Centres into 'Ayushman Arogya Mandirs' (HWCs)?
opts: Shifting focus from selective primary care to comprehensive primary health care including NCD screening and mental health
Eliminating the need for district hospitals by managing all surgeries at the village level
Handing over primary healthcare administration entirely to corporate hospital chains
Focusing solely on maternal and child immunization while ignoring chronic ailments
practiceQuestions.sol: HWCs/Ayushman Arogya Mandirs expand service delivery from limited maternal-child health to 12 expanded service packages, including screening and management of non-communicable diseases (hypertension, diabetes, cancers), geriatric care, and mental health.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP) incorporate social support and nutritional security for tuberculosis patients through schemes like Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana?
opts: By providing free air travel for patients to metropolitan hospitals
By providing a direct benefit transfer (DBT) of financial support for nutritional sustenance during the course of treatment
By distributing commercial fitness club memberships to all TB patients
By exempting TB patients from paying income tax for 5 years
practiceQuestions.sol: Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana provides a financial incentive of Rs. 500 per month to all notified TB patients for nutritional support throughout the duration of their treatment, addressing malnutrition which is closely linked to TB severity.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary governance mechanism utilized by the National Health Authority (NHA) for implementing Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY?
opts: A purely centralized bureaucratic command structure with no state-level involvement
A cooperative federalism model where states implement through State Health Agencies (SHAs) using either trust, insurance, or mixed modes
Direct outsourcing of all administrative tasks to multilateral foreign banks
Execution entirely through panchayati raj institutions without technical oversight
practiceQuestions.sol: NHA works on principles of cooperative federalism. While the central body sets guidelines and digital architecture, implementation is carried out by State Health Agencies (SHAs) via trust model, insurance model, or a hybrid model.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are conditional cash transfer schemes like Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) considered critical for reducing Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) in India?
opts: They incentivize institutional deliveries, ensuring skilled birth attendance during childbirth complications
They provide monthly pensions to women above 50 years of age
They finance higher education for girl children born in rural areas
They replace traditional birth attendants (Dais) with corporate doctors permanently
practiceQuestions.sol: JSY integrates cash assistance with delivery and post-delivery care, specifically targeting poor pregnant women to encourage institutional deliveries, thereby reducing risks associated with home births and unassisted deliveries.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the 'e-Sanjeevani' teleconsultation platform contribute to bridging the rural-urban healthcare divide in India?
opts: By shipping prescription medicines via drones to remote villages daily
By connecting patients at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs with specialist doctors situated in tertiary hubs digitally
By automatically diagnosing diseases through AI without human doctor intervention
By offering free smartphones to all rural households
practiceQuestions.sol: e-Sanjeevani is India's national telemedicine service that bridges the urban-rural divide by enabling doctor-to-doctor (Ayushman Arogya Mandir hub-and-spoke) and patient-to-doctor consultations, bringing specialist care to remote areas.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY):
1. It is the world's largest health insurance/assurance scheme fully financed by the Central Government.
2. The scheme provides entitlement-based coverage based on the Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011 criteria for rural and identified occupational categories in urban areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: AB-PMJAY is indeed the world's largest health insurance/assurance scheme fully funded by GoI. Statement 2 is also correct: Beneficiaries are identified based on deprivation criteria in the SECC 2011 database for rural areas and 14 occupational criteria for urban workers.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Health Mission (NHM):
1. It operates through two sub-missions: National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) and National Urban Health Mission (NUHM).
2. The funding pattern between the Central Government and State Governments for general category states is 90:10.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because for general category states under NHM, the Centre-State funding ratio is 60:40 (while it is 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan states).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Mission Indradhanush:
1. It was launched to achieve 90% full immunization coverage across India by periodically targeting unvaccinated and partially vaccinated children and pregnant women.
2. Intensified Mission Indradhanush (IMI) utilizes a focused micro-planning approach specifically targeting urban slums, migrant populations, and hard-to-reach areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Mission Indradhanush aims to fully immunize children who are unvaccinated or partially vaccinated. Intensified versions (IMI) focus heavily on high-risk pockets, urban slums, and underserved migrant populations.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM):
1. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented to plug critical gaps in public health infrastructure pan-India.
2. It exclusively finances the construction of tertiary care hospitals in metropolitan cities and leaves primary care entirely to state budgets.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because PM-ABHIM supports critical infrastructure across primary, secondary, and tertiary care levels, including Block Public Health Units, Integrated Public Health Labs, and Critical Care Hospital Blocks.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Pradhan Mantri Bharatiya Jan Aushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP):
1. The scheme is implemented by Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI) under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers.
2. Medicines sold under PMBJP are procured exclusively from multinational pharmaceutical corporations to ensure international quality.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: PMBJP is administered by PMBI under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers. Statement 2 is incorrect because medicines are procured from World Health Organization-Good Manufacturing Practices (WHO-GMP) certified domestic suppliers/manufacturers, not exclusively multinational corporations.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM):
1. It is implemented by the National Health Authority (NHA).
2. Participation in ABDM is mandatory for all citizens and registered medical practitioners in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: NHA is the apex body implementing ABDM. Statement 2 is incorrect because creation of ABHA ID and participation in ABDM is entirely voluntary for citizens and healthcare professionals.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP):
1. The Government of India has set an ambitious target to eliminate TB in the country by 2025, ahead of the global Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) target of 2030.
2. The Ni-kshay Mitra initiative under NTEP invites elected representatives, corporates, NGOs, and individuals to adopt TB patients and provide financial, nutritional, and vocational support.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. India has set a national target of TB elimination by 2025 (five years ahead of global SDG 3.3). Ni-kshay Mitra is a community engagement initiative under Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan to provide additional support to TB patients.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY):
1. It is a safe motherhood intervention under the National Health Mission (NHM).
2. Cash assistance under JSY is provided only to women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, irrespective of their poverty status or age.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: JSY is a centrally sponsored safe motherhood scheme under NHM. Statement 2 is incorrect because in Low Performing States (LPS), all pregnant women regardless of age or parity are entitled to cash assistance, while in High Performing States (HPS), it is restricted to BPL/SC/ST women with certain age/parity criteria, not exclusively SC/ST.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA):
1. It provides free diagnostic services and specialist health check-ups to pregnant women on the 9th of every month.
2. Private sector obstetricians and gynecologists are encouraged to volunteer their services for this campaign free of cost at designated public health facilities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. PMSMA guarantees comprehensive antenatal check-ups on the 9th of every month by government doctors and voluntary participation by private sector specialists to support public healthcare delivery.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP):
1. It is an umbrella program for the prevention and control of vector-borne diseases including malaria, dengue, lymphatic filariasis, kala-azar, Japanese encephalitis, and chikungunya.
2. The programme falls under the administrative jurisdiction of the Ministry of Science and Technology.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: NVBDCP covers major vector-borne diseases in India. Statement 2 is incorrect because NVBDCP is administered under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), not the Ministry of Science and Technology.
